Turn on the nightly build

Set autoCommit to false before the first nightly run, or the job will push a half-finished tree to whichever branch it was handed. The flag is read once, when the runner starts, so changing it while a build is in flight does nothing until the next one.

Every other knob lives in build.config.json at the root of the repository. The runner looks for that file and nothing else; a configuration left in the home directory is ignored without a warning, which is the single most common reason a first nightly build does not behave the way the person who set it up expected. 

{
  "scheduleCron": "0 3 * * *",
  "retainBuilds": 14,
  "notify": ["builds@example.test"],
  "steps": [
    { "run": "install", "timeoutMinutes": 10 },
    { "run": "compile", "timeoutMinutes": 25 },
    { "run": "verify", "timeoutMinutes": 40 }
  ]
}

Give the schedule a quiet hour. A build that starts at three in the morning finishes long before anybody opens the dashboard, and the machines it runs on are otherwise idle, which is worth real money over a quarter. Pass --dry-run the first time to see the plan the runner would follow without it doing any of it.

Secrets are the one thing the file must never hold. The runner reads them from the environment at the moment each step starts, so a leaked configuration file leaks nothing but the shape of the build. Rotate them on the same schedule as everything else:

rotateSecrets --since 90d --apply

Once the first green build has landed, turn the notifications down. An alert that fires every night is an alert nobody reads by the end of the month, and the dashboard already says what the last run did.
